text:
mona: Quick flag  bringing up Karst-11B-slim (4-bit asymmetric quant) for a latency tier. Before spinning up any customer-facing endpoints: need a legal read on redistribution/sublicense and how to surface attribution in Console.

ravi: short tech summary  4-bit quant reduces token cost ~3x, p95 latency ~2.4x better. Eval shows small drop on multi-turn coherence (-2.7%) and a few prompt families where beam diversity drops.

mona: upstream LICENSE has a chunky paragraph mentioning "derivative binaries" and a "no-hosting without commercial license" clause. Pasted excerpt below.

ci-bot: ```
KARST RESEARCH LICENSE 1.2
- Research and evaluation allowed for noncommercial use.
- Redistribution of model weights or derivative binaries is prohibited without explicit permission.
- Hosting model functionality as part of a paid service requires a separate commercial license.
- Transformations (quantization, pruning, conversion) are considered Derivative Works unless explicitly waived.
- Attribution: Derivative Works must include credit and a link to the original license.
```

alex (legal): TL;DR  two issues: (1) license treats quantized formats as derivatives (so redistribution/hosting needs permission), (2) hosting-for-pay clause likely blocks our hosted API for paying customers. Attribution is straightforward but secondary.

ravi: operationally we don't export quant binaries; runtime holds tensors in memory. Does "redistribution of model weights" vs "hosting" differ?

alex (legal): yes, but both are covered. Serving outputs to paying users is "hosting model functionality". Even if we never hand out the binary, offering inference behind a paid endpoint triggers that clause.

mona: product question  if we get permission, what's the minimal attribution UX? Model card plus a small "powered by" line in Console?

alex (legal): that should be fine: persistent model metadata card with name + license link + a visible "powered by Karst Research" on the model selector or endpoint docs. Also include full redistribution notice in legal docs. We'll confirm exact wording in outreach.

carmen: fallback ideas: (A) keep quantized builds internal for benchmarking + Private demos, block hosted; (B) offer BYO (customer uploads their own Karst binary into Private/VPC); (C) ask upstream for a hosting carve-out or commercial license.

mona: action items: (1) ravi upload full LICENSE and commit hash to onboarding folder; (2) alex + legal draft outreach asking for (a) permission to host quant runtime for paying customers, (b) clarify whether in-memory quant is treated as derivative, (c) acceptable attribution text, (d) any commercial terms; (3) ravi include exact quant method + storage/docs for runtime.

ravi: added perf CSV and quant pipeline doc to /onboard/karst-11b-slim. Technical blurb for outreach: AWQ-like asymmetric 4-bit, per-channel scales, shards encrypted, never publicly published; can confirm rollback/fallback to FP16.

ci-bot: policy reminder  set onboarding field "legal:pending" and block publish flag until cleared.

alex (legal): we'll draft the outreach today and propose the attribution string. If upstream declines hosting for pay, product will mark model as "hosted:ineligible" and push BYO/private paths.

mona: thanks all  keeping thread open for any quick clarifications. :wave:
